primary.body:
## Intent Make the operator COMPLETE decoupled / out-of-band (app-push) 3-D Secure, not just detect it. Today the operator detects the 3DS challenge and waits, but for banks that authenticate the challenge OUT OF BAND (in a mobile banking app, decoupled 3DS) it never receives the completion, so the order never finalizes even though the bank authenticated successfully. Live reproduction (3x, 2026-08-14): Merchant KobeeJapan (store.kobeejapan.net), single-page Shopify checkout, DBS Mastercard (vaulted), rc.21 installed (has #516 checkout fix + 3DS detection). Operator fills card, submits, Stripe requires 3DS -> Stripe hosted challenge renders in a CardinalCommerce iframe (https://hooks.stripe.com/3d_secure_2/hosted?...payment_intent=pi_...&payment_intent_client_secret=...&publishable_key=pk_live_...&stripe_account=acct_...). DBS uses decoupled/app-push 3DS: bank pushes to mobile app, user approves in-app out of band, bank/ACS authenticates OOB. Bug: operator's in-browser challenge frame never receives that OOB completion -- operate_pay's three_ds_wait_seconds elapses and returns payment_3ds_required/needs_user (wall=3ds, resume=checkout). Checkout stays stuck on Cardinal frame + Processing, no order is created, authenticated-but-uncaptured PaymentIntent expires uncaptured. Verified the user approved the push immediately and it still never registered -- not a timing/latency problem, a missing completion path. Root cause (confirmed via code read, not just hypothesis): the operator's 3DS handling (apps/mcp/src/bot/browser.ts detectThreeDsChallenge/waitForThreeDsResolution; apps/mcp/src/bot/pay-operator.ts 3DS state machine) only detected/finalized the IN-FRAME challenge-render case (user completes inside the iframe) via DOM text/URL heuristics, never the DECOUPLED case where completion is signalled server-side (Stripe transitions the PaymentIntent out of requires_action after the ACS confirms OOB). It waited on an in-frame signal that never arrives for app-push banks. Fix implemented: during the 3DS wait, additionally poll the authoritative Stripe PaymentIntent status -- the client_secret + publishable_key are already present in the challenge_url, parsed with a new parseStripeChallengeParams helper (publishable key only, never the secret key -- the same public retrieve-with-client-secret call Stripe.js itself makes client-side). Chose PaymentIntent polling over polling Shopify's own checkout-completion internals because it's the same signal Stripe's SDK relies on, requires no per-merchant-theme reverse engineering, and needs no additional credentials. When the PaymentIntent status leaves requires_action to succeeded/processing/requires_capture (classifyStripePaymentIntentStatus), that's treated as OOB-authenticated: the checkout page is reloaded once so the merchant's own completion logic re-evaluates now-authoritative server state, then the EXISTING DOM-based success detection (unchanged, still covers the in-frame case) gets a bounded ~30s grace window to confirm real order completion. requires_payment_method/canceled PaymentIntent statuses are treated as a definitive failure. Fail-closed: if the grace window elapses without a genuine DOM completion signal, the code returns a new distinct outcome (authenticated_pending_order -> payment_3ds_authenticated_pending_order) with needs_user guidance instead of ever silently claiming merchant/amount success on an unconfirmed completion. The original in-frame 3DS path (existing DOM text/URL detection) is completely unchanged and additive only. Money-fence boundaries preserved: single-approval-per-purchase unchanged, one approval authorizes exactly one charge, no re-arm/duplicate/double-charge path added, card only ever opens inside operate_pay, SecretRef.stored:false unaffected, card never exposed to the model. #515 session-addressed payments and the #516 checkout fix + detection + fail-closed confirmation are preserved -- this change is additive to the existing 3DS wait, not a replacement. Tests added: apps/mcp/src/bot/__tests__/browser-payment.test.ts (Stripe challenge URL parsing incl. non-Stripe-host and missing-param refusal, PaymentIntent status classification table, OOB polling+reload+fail-closed-pending, OOB polling+reload+genuine-DOM-success, OOB polling+terminal-failure-status with no reload, and a guard that the ordinary in-frame path never polls Stripe or reloads when no challenge_url is present) and apps/mcp/src/bot/__tests__/pay-operator.test.ts (new payment_3ds_authenticated_pending_order status end to end, plus updated existing waitForThreeDsResolution call-signature assertions for the new challenge_url argument). All 70 mcp test files / 1288 tests pass; typecheck clean. The definitive proof is a LIVE retry against a real DBS app-push 3DS challenge, which will be run separately with the captain after merge -- state that in the PR body. Deliver as a PR to staging (not main). Do NOT bump the package version -- that is published separately. ## What Changed - Poll Stripe PaymentIntent status during Stripe-hosted 3DS waits, keep challenge execution active, and reload the checkout once after an observed out-of-band authentication transition so merchant completion logic can resume. - Preserve merchant DOM confirmation as the success gate; treat terminal Stripe failures as declines and return `payment_3ds_authenticated_pending_order` with manual-check warnings and repeat-payment blocking when no order is confirmed. - Add regression coverage and documentation for decoupled 3DS parsing, polling, reload, failure, and fail-closed paths. A live DBS app-push retry will be run separately with the captain after merge. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The source is fail-closed and intent-conformant, but this money-path change depends on live browser and issuer timing whose definitive DBS verification is explicitly deferred until after merge. ## Testing The supplied baseline was successful; focused browser/operator tests, an executable OOB status-transition simulation, a real Chrome launch-flag probe, and a real-browser foreground submission check all passed, while the explicitly planned live DBS app-push retry remains separate post-merge proof with the captain.
Evidence: Executable OOB 3DS scenario transcript `App-push + merchant confirmation → succeeded (2 Stripe polls, 1 reload); app-push without merchant confirmation → authenticated_pending_order (1 reload); issuer rejection → failed (no reload); ordinary in-frame challenge → timeout (no Stripe polling or reload).` ```text {"scenario":"app-push authenticated and merchant confirms order","resolution":"succeeded","stripe_status_polls":2,"checkout_reloads":1} {"scenario":"app-push authenticated but merchant never confirms order","resolution":"authenticated_pending_order","stripe_status_polls":4,"checkout_reloads":1} {"scenario":"issuer rejects authentication","resolution":"failed","stripe_status_polls":2,"checkout_reloads":0} {"scenario":"ordinary in-frame challenge without Stripe challenge URL","resolution":"timeout","stripe_status_polls":0,"checkout_reloads":0} ```

Preserve and validate the account ID and include it in the retrieval request. See [Stripe connected-account authentication](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/authentication). - 🚨 `apps/mcp/src/bot/pay-operator.ts:1299` - The requirement says to make the operator complete OOB 3DS, but only the single-page path passes `challenge_url` and handles `authenticated_pending_order`. The split-checkout confirm path at line 1529 still calls the resolver without the URL and cannot poll/reload; it also lacks mapping for the new result, while its session wrapper does not clear that new terminal status. Route both submit paths through the same challenge-resolution boundary and update confirm lifecycle handling. - ⚠️ `apps/mcp/src/bot/pay-operator.ts:1307` - The new fail-closed status is audited, but the activity consumer classifies only names matching `declin|fail|reject|outcome_unknown` as problematic. `payment_3ds_authenticated_pending_order` therefore appears as a normal green “Payment,” contradicting the operator’s warning that order completion is unconfirmed. Give this status an explicit pending/warning presentation. 🔧 Fix: Harden decoupled 3DS completion across payment paths 2 warnings still open: - ⚠️ `apps/mcp/src/bot/browser.ts:10051` - The 30-second confirmation grace period starts before the awaited reload. A slow reload can consume the entire window, causing `authenticated_pending_order` even when the reload lands on a genuine order-completion route because that route is not rechecked before the deadline branch. Start the grace period after reload settles, or recheck the checkout outcome immediately afterward. - ⚠️ `apps/mcp/src/tools/operate-pay.ts:248` - Both new terminal-state branches omit `recordActivePaymentProvenance`, whose existing status guard only covers `payment_submitted` and `payment_3ds_required`. If a manual check later confirms the order and the run is remembered, the recorded recipe can omit the `operate_pay` step and card provenance. Include `payment_3ds_authenticated_pending_order` in the provenance condition for both split and single-page flows. 🔧 Fix: Preserve OOB grace timing and payment provenance 1 error still open: - 🚨 `apps/mcp/src/bot/browser.ts:10012` - Stripe polling parameters are parsed only once from the initially detected `challengeUrl`. `detectThreeDsChallenge` can detect a structural child iframe or DBS text in an ancestor frame and return that ancestor’s URL, while the nested `hooks.stripe.com` frame loads later. Parsing then remains undefined forever, so polling never starts and the original OOB timeout remains reachable. Discover the active parseable Stripe challenge URL during the wait until captured, then freeze it to that transaction; cover nested and late-navigating challenge frames. 🔧 Fix: Keep decoupled 3DS challenges active and discoverable 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `AGENTS.md:405` - The new durable guidance says decoupled authentication completes entirely out of band and presents PaymentIntent polling/reload as the fix, but the later live diagnostic established that the Cardinal iframe must remain active to finish its post-approval handshake. Document the three background-throttling flags, `bringToFront()` calls, and the poll's classifier-only role so future maintenance does not preserve the wrong invariant and regress the actual fix. - ℹ️ `AGENTS.md:425` - This adds a second “Maintaining this file” section immediately after the existing one. Merge its useful sentences into the first section to keep the repository contract concise and non-duplicative. 🔧 Fix: Correct 3DS guidance and deduplicate maintenance rules 1 warning still open: - ⚠️ `skills/trusty-squire/SKILL.md:110` - The new public terminal status is missing from the agent-facing payment safety contract. This skill only prohibits blind resubmission for `payment_outcome_unknown`, while README.md:75 and SECURITY.md:165 still imply every unconfirmed 3DS flow returns that older status. After the session ends, a host following these docs may retry `payment_3ds_authenticated_pending_order` without the required manual order check. Document the new status alongside `payment_outcome_unknown`, explicitly forbidding success claims and blind resubmission. 🔧 Fix: Document pending 3DS manual-check safety contract ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

commit.message:
fix(security): eliminate os command injection across smart_* tools (#169)

* fix(security): eliminate os command injection across smart_* tools

Addresses GHSA-29p3-56wx-ggfh (critical), GHSA-8w8q-fgv9-j286,
GHSA-49mq-fc6q-3h46, and GHSA-76pc-mqxp-3rq5.

- Add src/utils/safe-exec.ts argv-mode helpers (execFileSafe/Sync, spawnSafe)
  plus assertSafeGitRef / assertSafePathArg / assertSafeArg / assertAllowed.
- smart_diff/branch/log/merge/status: replace every execSync string command
  with argv-mode execFileSafeSync; validate refs and paths (GHSA-29p3).
- smart_install: allowlist packageManager, reject option-flag package specs,
  spawn with shell:false (GHSA-8w8q).
- smart_user: route all lookups through argv-mode execFileSafe, replace
  getent||grep/cat pipelines with in-process fallbacks (GHSA-49mq).
- web-server: validate sessionId against ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ on both
  session-summary and session-events endpoints (GHSA-76pc path traversal).
- CallTool handler now routes validated args downstream; remove ts-expect-error.
- Tighten zod schemas for the affected tools (defense-in-depth).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): convert remaining shell sinks to argv mode + add tests

Completes the full audit recommended by GHSA-29p3-56wx-ggfh. Converts every
remaining string-command / shell:true sink across the tool surface to argv-mode
execution and validates caller-controlled inputs:

- build-systems: smart-logs (in-process file tail + argv system logs),
  smart-network (ping host validation), smart-system-metrics (df path),
  smart-build/lint/test/typecheck/docker (shell:false + npx/npm .cmd on win),
  smart-processes (wmic/ps argv).
- system-operations: smart-service (all systemctl/sc/docker control + info ops),
  smart-process (wmic/ps/pstree argv + pid/name validation),
  smart-cron (crontab via stdin, schtasks argv, journalctl argv).
- code-analysis: smart-ast-grep (argv, no command-string concat).
- configuration: smart-package-json (npm/yarn/pnpm list/audit/outdated argv).
- Export isValidSessionId for testing.
- Add tests/unit/security: validator + argv-neutralization + schema-rejection
  + path-traversal regression tests (20 tests).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): address review feedback, formatting, and weak-hash alerts

- align web-server session-id pattern with the mcp validator (allow dots)
- drop gnu-only ps --no-headers flag for macos compatibility
- stop passing description as a second /tn flag to schtasks
- replace md5 cache-key hashing with sha256 in smart-user (codeql js/weak-cryptographic-algorithm)
- run prettier on the files flagged by the lint and format check

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): standardize session-id validation on the strict no-dot pattern

the review suggestion aligned web-server with index.ts by allowing dots,
but the regression test intentionally rejects dotted ids (a.b, ..) and
session ids are generated as alphanumeric/dash tokens, so dots are never
legitimate. align both validators on ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(security): resolve remaining codeql and dependabot alerts

- web-server: add express-rate-limit (300 req/min) in front of all routes
  (js/missing-rate-limiting) and prove jsonl log paths stay inside the
  hooks data dir via resolve+relative containment (js/path-injection).
- smart-test: escape every regex metacharacter including backslash in a
  single pass before building the jest pattern (js/incomplete-sanitization).
- smart-ast-grep: strip all wildcards from exclude patterns, not just the
  first (js/incomplete-sanitization).
- smart-pretty: strip html tags to a fixpoint so nested tags cannot
  survive a single pass (js/incomplete-multi-character-sanitization).
- deps: hoist npm@^11.16.0 so semantic-release no longer pulls the
  bundled vulnerable brace-expansion@5.0.4 / ip-address@10.1.0
  (dependabot 75 and 83); npm audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: franklinic <franklin@ivorycloud.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

primary.body:
## Summary
Closes remaining checklist items from #35 (PR1–PR4 policy conversion review):
- **Security:** OPA uses `input.attributes.source.address` (not XFF); apiKey/appIdKey Secrets scoped to target namespace; blank CIDRs skipped with warn
- **Bugs:** CORS Allow-Credentials indent aligned; incomplete `token_introspection` no longer emits mismatched oauth2 Secret
- **Docs:** WARNING comments for connection_limiters→rate, leaky_bucket→fixed window, plan ceiling = max across plans
- **Style:** FQN→imports; drop unused `@SuppressWarnings` on `edgeLimiterName`

Already fixed on main (no-op): #6 packageGrows assertion, #11 redundant boolean, #14 ConversionServiceTest reflection, #15 Japanese README.  
**Deferred:** #7 YAML string-concat rewrite (high blast radius).

## Linked Issue
Closes #35

## Test plan
- [x] `mvn -Dtest=ConversionServiceTest test` (80 tests)
- [ ] Full backend CI on this PR
- [ ] Spot-check generated OPA Rego / AuthPolicy Secret selectors / CORS YAML indent

## Notes for @pcastelo
- Authorino must populate `source.address` at runtime (no XFF fallback by design).
- Dropping `allNamespaces` may break demos that rely on cross-namespace Secrets.


Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

## Summary
- store a SHA-256 content digest alongside the existing artifact entry digest for newly added files and checksum-enabled local file references
- prefer SHA-256 for local artifact download, cache-hit, and verify integrity checks while preserving legacy MD5 compatibility for older entries
- include SHA-256 metadata in artifact manifest digests when available and propagate it through artifact references

Closes #12030

commit.message:
fix: [security] stop resolving strings to markup; sanitize UI svg icons

tryResolveHTMLElement parsed any string as HTML and appended it live, which is
how untrusted properties became XSS. Strings now resolve to text, matching the
1.4.0 PropertyEntry rule; return an element to render HTML. Drops the dead
createHtmlDL that fed it, and runs createIcon's svgIcon through the sanitizer.

- As reported by Jeroen Pinoy

primary.body:
## Summary

- Protect all five server-controlled Realtime error fields (`message`, `code`, `param`, `type`, and `event_id`) with exception-safe string conversion in the stable and beta handwritten Realtime emitters.
- Preserve existing valid-error formatting, the original event/error metadata, documented asynchronous rejection for unhandled errors, and exceptions thrown by application error listeners.
- Add one dedicated handwritten regression suite covering the four public stable/beta × native/Node WebSocket clients.

## Security impact

A remote WebSocket peer that can deliver a valid JSON Realtime error frame can send a noncoercible error value, for example:

```json
{"type":"error","error":{"message":{"toString":null,"valueOf":null}}}
```

The existing formatter interpolates attacker-controlled values before invoking registered SDK error handlers. JavaScript coercion then throws `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value`; Node WebSocket clients can consequently terminate through an uncaught exception even when an SDK `.on('error')` listener is registered. The same sink exists for all five error fields in both stable and beta clients. The impact is remotely triggerable client denial of service, not credential disclosure or authentication bypass.

The fix catches only conversion failures and substitutes `[unserializable error value]`. It does not serialize untrusted objects, change public APIs, swallow application listener exceptions, or modify transport/generated files.

## Verification

- Failure-first baseline on unchanged `main`: **32 failing / 20 passing** security cases, reproducing every field across all four public clients.
- `pnpm test tests/realtime-error-payload-security.test.ts --reporter=dot` — **52/52 passed**.
- `pnpm run test:unit --reporter=dot` — **2,142/2,142 passed across 71 handwritten test files**.
- `pnpm run lint` — passed.
- `pnpm exec tsc` — passed.
- `pnpm run build` — passed, including CommonJS/ESM package smoke checks.
- Verified every changed file lacks the Castiron generated-file header and is absent from the generated/legacy-file manifest.
- Refreshed all open-PR changed-file lists immediately before publication; none overlaps these three handwritten files.

+# Coupon CMS — Phase 1 (Admin Foundation)
+
+A production-ready **Admin CMS** foundation for a coupon website, built with Laravel, Blade, Tailwind CSS and Alpine.js.
+
+This phase ships the admin side only — authentication, dashboard, Stores/Categories/Coupons management, media uploads, admin users, roles, activity logs and settings. The public coupon website, affiliate tracking, automated importing and SEO automation are intentionally out of scope and will be built on top of this foundation in later phases.
+
+## Tech Stack
+
+- PHP 8.2+
+- Laravel 13 (11/12-compatible application structure)
+- MySQL 8+
+- Blade templates, Tailwind CSS, Alpine.js
+- Laravel Auth, Migrations, Eloquent, Form Requests, Policies/Gates, Storage
+- Vite
+
+## Features
+
+- Secure admin authentication (login, logout, remember me, forgot/reset password, login throttling, session security) scoped to a dedicated `admin` guard and `admin_users` table
+- Collapsible sidebar / topbar SaaS-style admin layout with a reusable Blade UI kit (buttons, inputs, selects, tables, modals, alerts, badges, pagination, empty states, confirmation dialogs)
+- Dashboard with store/category/coupon stats, recent records and quick actions
+- Full CRUD for Stores, Categories (parent/child) and Coupons, each with search/filter/sort, server-side pagination, status & featured toggles, and SEO placeholder fields
+- Coupon classification (discount type, coupon type, new-user/app-only/bank-offer/student tags), verified/exclusive/featured flags, and a non-destructive "expired" indicator based on `expiry_date`
+- Reusable, security-conscious media upload service (safe random filenames, real MIME-type validation, JPG/PNG/WebP only) plus a Media Library
+- Admin user management with role-based access (Super Admin vs Manager) and self-lockout protection
+- Activity log of admin actions (who, what, when, IP, user agent) with filters
+- Global settings (general, basic SEO defaults, system) backed by a key/value store
+- Custom 404/403/419/422/500 error pages
+
+## Requirements
+
+- PHP 8.2+
+- Composer 2
+- Node.js 18+ and npm
+- MySQL 8+ (or SQLite for quick local trials)
+
+## Installation
+
+```bash
+git clone <repository-url> coupon-cms
+cd coupon-cms
+
+composer install
+npm install
+```
+
+## Environment Setup
+
+```bash
+cp .env.example .env
+php artisan key:generate
+```
+
+Edit `.env` and set your database credentials (MySQL is the default in `.env.example`):
+
+```env
+DB_CONNECTION=mysql
+DB_HOST=127.0.0.1
+DB_PORT=3306
+DB_DATABASE=coupon_cms
+DB_USERNAME=root
+DB_PASSWORD=
+```
+
+> Quick local trial without MySQL: set `DB_CONNECTION=sqlite` and run `touch database/database.sqlite`.
+
+Optionally set the seeded super admin's credentials before seeding (defaults shown):
+
+```env
+SEED_ADMIN_NAME="Super Admin"
+SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.com
+SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD=ChangeMe123!
+```
+
+## Database Setup
+
+Create the database (MySQL example):
+
+```bash
+mysql -u root -p -e "CREATE DATABASE coupon_cms CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;"
+```
+
+## Migration Commands
+
+```bash
+php artisan migrate            # run migrations
+php artisan migrate:fresh      # drop all tables and re-run (destructive, dev only)
+```
+
+## Seeder Commands
+
+```bash
+php artisan db:seed
+```
+
+This creates:
+
+- A **Super Admin** (`SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, defaults `admin@example.com` / `ChangeMe123!`) and a demo **Manager** (`manager@example.com` / `ChangeMe123!`)
+- 10 top-level categories (Fashion, Electronics, Travel, Food, Beauty, Hosting, Software, Grocery, Home & Kitchen, Sports) with a few child categories
+- 6 demo stores (Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, AJIO, Nykaa, Hostinger India)
+- A handful of coupons per store, clearly titled `[DEMO] ...` and flagged in their description as test/demo data — **not real, working coupon codes**
+
+Run both migrations and seeders from a clean database in one go:
+
+```bash
+php artisan migrate:fresh --seed
+```
+
+**Change the seeded admin passwords immediately after first login in any shared/production environment.**
+
+## Storage Setup
+
+Uploaded files (store logos, category images, coupon/OG images, the Media Library) are written to the `public` disk. Link it so uploads are web-accessible:
+
+```bash
+php artisan storage:link
+```
+
+## Development Commands
+
+```bash
+npm run dev          # Vite dev server with hot reload
+php artisan serve    # PHP dev server (http://127.0.0.1:8000)
+```
+
+Or run both together:
+
+```bash
+composer run dev
+```
+
+Log in at `/admin/login` with the seeded admin credentials.
+
+## Production Deployment Notes
+
+- Set `APP_ENV=production`, `APP_DEBUG=false`, and a strong, unique `APP_KEY`
+- Serve over HTTPS; `SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE` should be `true` behind HTTPS
+- Run `npm run build` to compile production assets (do **not** run `npm run dev` in production)
+- Run `composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader`
+- Run `php artisan migrate --force` (never `migrate:fresh` against production data)
+- Run `php artisan config:cache route:cache view:cache`
+- Ensure `storage/` and `bootstrap/cache/` are writable by the web server
+- Confirm `php artisan storage:link` has been run so uploaded media is servable
+- Never commit `.env` — keep DB credentials, `APP_KEY`, mail credentials and future affiliate/API keys out of source control
+
+## Default Admin Login
+
+After seeding, log in at `/admin/login`:
+
+| Role | Email | Password |
+|---|---|---|
+| Super Admin | `admin@example.com` (or `SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL`) | `ChangeMe123!` (or `SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD`) |
+| Manager (demo) | `manager@example.com` | `ChangeMe123!` |
+
+Super Admins have full access, including Admin Users and Settings. Managers can manage Stores, Categories and Coupons but not Admin Users or Settings.
+
+## Roles & Permissions
+
+Authorization is implemented with Laravel Policies and Gates (`App\Policies\*`, `Gate::before` in `AppServiceProvider`) rather than a permissions package, so additional roles can be introduced later without a rewrite.
+
+## Project Structure Notes
+
+- Admin routes live in `routes/admin.php` (prefixed `/admin`, named `admin.*`), kept separate from `routes/web.php`, which is reserved for the public coupon website built in a later phase.
+- `App\Enums` holds the fixed vocabularies (`Status`, `AdminRole`, `DiscountType`, `CouponType`) so coupon/store types aren't hard-coded across the app.
+- `App\Services` holds `SlugService` (unique slug generation), `MediaUploadService` (secure uploads), `ActivityLogService` and `SettingsService`, so future phases can reuse or extend them without touching controllers.
+- SEO fields (`meta_title`, `meta_description`, `canonical_url`, `robots_index`, `robots_follow`, `og_*`) exist on categories/stores/coupons now so Phase 3's SEO engine has data to work with, but no SEO rendering logic ships in Phase 1.
+
+## What's Not in Phase 1
+
+By design, this phase does **not** include the public coupon website, affiliate network integrations, automated coupon importing/verification, cashback, public user accounts, or programmatic SEO generation. The database and architecture are intentionally left room to add these in later phases (see the SEO/affiliate placeholder fields and the `routes/web.php` split).

+<?php

+namespace App\Http\Requests\Admin;
+
+use App\Enums\CouponType;
+use App\Enums\DiscountType;
+use App\Enums\Status;
+use App\Models\Coupon;
+use Illuminate\Foundation\Http\FormRequest;
+use Illuminate\Validation\Rule;
+
+class CouponRequest extends FormRequest
+{
+    public function authorize(): bool
+    {
+        return true;
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * @return array<string, mixed>
+     */
+    public function rules(): array
+    {
+        /** @var Coupon|null $coupon */
+        $coupon = $this->route('coupon');
+
+        return [
+            'store_id' => ['required', Rule::exists('stores', 'id')->whereNull('deleted_at')],
+            'category_id' => ['nullable', Rule::exists('categories', 'id')->whereNull('deleted_at')],
+            'title' => ['required', 'string', 'max:255'],
+            'slug' => [
+                'nullable', 'string', 'max:255', 'alpha_dash',
+                Rule::unique('coupons', 'slug')->ignore($coupon)->withoutTrashed(),
+            ],
+            'code' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:100'],
+            'description' => ['nullable', 'string'],
+
+            'discount_type' => ['required', Rule::enum(DiscountType::class)],
+            'discount_value' => ['nullable', 'numeric', 'min:0'],
+            'minimum_order' => ['nullable', 'numeric', 'min:0'],
+            'maximum_discount' => ['nullable', 'numeric', 'min:0'],
+
+            'start_date' => ['nullable', 'date'],
+            'expiry_date' => ['nullable', 'date', 'after_or_equal:start_date'],
+
+            'coupon_type' => ['required', Rule::enum(CouponType::class)],
+            'is_new_user' => ['sometimes', 'boolean'],
+            'is_app_only' => ['sometimes', 'boolean'],
+            'is_bank_offer' => ['sometimes', 'boolean'],
+            'is_student' => ['sometimes', 'boolean'],
+
+            'affiliate_url' => ['nullable', 'url', 'max:255'],
+
+            'status' => ['required', Rule::enum(Status::class)],
+            'featured' => ['sometimes', 'boolean'],
+            'exclusive' => ['sometimes', 'boolean'],
+            'verified' => ['sometimes', 'boolean'],
+            'sort_order' => ['nullable', 'integer', 'min:0'],
+
+            'meta_title' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:255'],
+            'meta_description' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:500'],
+            'canonical_url' => ['nullable', 'url', 'max:255'],
+            'robots_index' => ['sometimes', 'boolean'],
+            'robots_follow' => ['sometimes', 'boolean'],
+            'og_title' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:255'],
+            'og_description' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:500'],
+            'og_image' => ['nullable', 'image', 'mimes:jpg,jpeg,png,webp', 'max:'.config('media.max_size_kb')],
+        ];
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * @return array<string, mixed>
+     */
+    public function validated($key = null, $default = null): array
+    {
+        $data = parent::validated($key, $default);
+
+        foreach (['is_new_user', 'is_app_only', 'is_bank_offer', 'is_student', 'featured', 'exclusive', 'verified', 'robots_index', 'robots_follow'] as $flag) {
+            $data[$flag] = $this->boolean($flag);
+        }
+
+        $data['sort_order'] = $data['sort_order'] ?? 0;
+
+        return $data;
+    }
+}

primary.body:
## Summary

Builds Phase 1 of the Coupon Website CMS: a production-ready **Admin CMS foundation** (Laravel 13 / Blade / Tailwind / Alpine), with the public coupon website and later-phase features (affiliate tracking, auto-import, etc.) intentionally left out but not blocked by the schema/architecture.

- Dedicated `admin` auth guard + `admin_users` table (separate from any future public user accounts) with login, logout, remember me, forgot/reset password, login throttling, and an `EnsureAdminIsActive` middleware guarding against mid-session deactivation
- Collapsible-sidebar SaaS-style admin layout (Alpine-driven) built from a reusable Blade UI kit: buttons, inputs, selects, tables, modals, alerts, badges, pagination, empty states, confirmation dialogs
- Dashboard with store/category/coupon stats, recent records and quick actions
- Full CRUD for **Stores**, **Categories** (parent/child) and **Coupons** — search/filter/sort, server-side pagination, status/featured/verified/exclusive toggles, unique slug generation (with manual override), SEO placeholder fields (`meta_*`, `canonical_url`, `robots_*`, `og_*`) for a later SEO phase
- Coupon classification (discount type, coupon type, new-user/app-only/bank-offer/student tags) via `App\Enums`, not hard-coded strings; non-destructive `is_expired` accessor based on `expiry_date`
- Reusable, security-conscious `MediaUploadService` (random filenames, real MIME-type validation, JPG/PNG/WebP only, no trust of client filenames/extensions) backing a Media Library plus inline store/category/coupon image uploads
- Admin User management with **Super Admin / Manager** roles enforced via Policies + `Gate::before`, and self-lockout protection (can't delete/deactivate your own logged-in account)
- Activity log audit trail (admin, action, module, record, description, IP, user agent) with filters
- Key/value **Settings** module (general / basic SEO / system)
- Custom 404/403/419/422/500/503 error pages
- Seeders: 10 categories (with children), 6 demo stores, a handful of coupons clearly marked `[DEMO]` / test data, a Super Admin + demo Manager
- Rewritten auth/profile test suite (18 passing tests) matching the new admin routes/guard

primary.body:
📌 Description

This PR fixes a broken access control vulnerability in api/graphql_schema.py:208-302 and api/main.py:195-197 where GraphQL resolvers exposed application data and mutations without authentication or authorization enforcement.

Previously, the GraphQL implementation trusted attacker-controlled identifiers directly and exposed the schema publicly:

Resolvers accepted attacker-controlled user_id and case_id parameters
No authentication dependency was enforced
No ownership validation was performed
Arbitrary user data could be queried directly
Mutations operated on attacker-supplied resource identifiers
graphiql=True exposed the full schema publicly

Because the GraphQL API trusted user-supplied identifiers without validating authenticated user context or ownership, unauthenticated callers could query or modify arbitrary application data.

Current behavior before the fix:

Any user’s case data could be queried without authorization
Sensitive documents and records were exposed publicly
Mutations could modify or delete arbitrary application data
Authorization scope depended entirely on attacker-controlled input
GraphQL resolvers bypassed application access control guarantees
Public schema exposure simplified endpoint enumeration and exploitation

If an attacker submitted crafted GraphQL queries or mutations with arbitrary user_id or case_id values, they could retrieve or manipulate data belonging to other users without authentication.

As a result:

Any user’s case data could be queried without authorization
Sensitive documents and records could be exposed publicly
Unauthorized mutations could modify or delete arbitrary data
GraphQL became a direct broken-access-control vector
Complete application data compromise became possible
Authorization guarantees became inconsistent across API surfaces

The updated implementation enforces authenticated access, validates ownership consistently, and restricts GraphQL exposure to authorized application contexts.

With these changes:

GraphQL endpoints now require authenticated access
Resolvers enforce ownership and authorization checks consistently
User identity derives from authenticated session context
Attacker-supplied identifiers no longer determine authorization scope
Unauthorized queries and mutations are rejected safely
Production deployments restrict unnecessary schema exposure features

✨ Changes Included

Added authentication enforcement for GraphQL endpoints
Integrated ownership validation into GraphQL resolvers
Removed reliance on attacker-controlled authorization identifiers
Restricted unauthorized query and mutation access
Hardened GraphQL access control behavior across resolvers
Disabled unnecessary schema exposure features for production environments

🧪 Testing Done

Verified unauthenticated GraphQL requests are rejected correctly
Tested ownership enforcement across query and mutation resolvers
Confirmed unauthorized resource access is blocked safely
Validated authenticated users can access only permitted resources
Tested GraphQL mutation authorization behavior
Confirmed no regressions in authorized GraphQL functionality

closes #1215

UPSERT/UPDATE-like writes against a nonexistent document URN are authorized as CREATE; writes against an existing document URN are authorized as UPDATE. Bridge documents additionally inherit VIEW (READ only) from the source entity when they have the `Bridge Document` subtype, a `bridge-*` ID, and resolvable source metadata; an unresolvable source fails closed unless direct document access already allowed the request. UPDATE and DELETE never inherit from the bridge source. **Action:** Grant document CREATE/EDIT/DELETE entity privileges or `MANAGE_DOCUMENTS` as needed; ensure readers have View Entity / Get Entity (or `MANAGE_DOCUMENTS`); do not rely on document unrestricted fail-open.
 - **(UI / Lineage)** The `LINEAGE_GRAPH_V2` and `LINEAGE_GRAPH_V3` feature flags (GMS environment variables) have been removed, along with the older lineage graph visualizations they gated. DataHub now always renders the latest lineage graph experience. **Action:** if you set `LINEAGE_GRAPH_V2` or `LINEAGE_GRAPH_V3` in your GMS environment or Helm values, remove them — they are no longer recognized. There is no longer a way to switch back to the previous lineage visualizations.

+"""
+E2E authorization smoke tests for container GraphQL view redaction (VBAC).
+
+Requires ``VIEW_AUTHORIZATION_ENABLED=true`` on GMS; skipped when view authorization is off.
+
+Covers:
+  - Direct ``container(urn)`` loads field-strip unauthorized containers (real URN retained)
+  - VIEW_ENTITY_PAGE on the container restores properties (e.g. description)
+  - ``parentContainers`` still returns unauthorized parents as field-stripped stubs
+"""
+
+import logging
+import uuid
+from typing import Any, Dict, Tuple
+
+import pytest
+
+from datahub.emitter.mcp import MetadataChangeProposalWrapper
+from datahub.metadata.schema_classes import ContainerClass, ContainerPropertiesClass
+from tests.authorization.utils import is_view_authorization_enabled
+from tests.consistency_utils import wait_for_writes_to_sync
+from tests.privileges.utils import (
+    clear_polices,
+    create_metadata_policy,
+    create_user,
+    remove_policy,
+    remove_user,
+    set_base_platform_privileges_policy_status,
+    set_view_dataset_sensitive_info_policy_status,
+    set_view_entity_profile_privileges_policy_status,
+)
+from tests.utils import (
+    get_frontend_session,
+    get_frontend_url,
+    login_as,
+    with_test_retry,
+)
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+pytestmark = [pytest.mark.no_cypress_suite1, pytest.mark.global_policy_mutator]
+
+_UNIQUE = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
+TEST_USER_EMAIL = f"container.view.auth.{_UNIQUE}@smoke.datahub.test"
+TEST_USER_URN = f"urn:li:corpuser:{TEST_USER_EMAIL}"
+TEST_USER_PASSWORD = "user"
+
+PARENT_CONTAINER_ID = f"vbac-parent-{_UNIQUE}"
+CHILD_CONTAINER_ID = f"vbac-child-{_UNIQUE}"
+PARENT_CONTAINER_URN = f"urn:li:container:{PARENT_CONTAINER_ID}"
+CHILD_CONTAINER_URN = f"urn:li:container:{CHILD_CONTAINER_ID}"
+
+PARENT_NAME = f"VBAC Parent {_UNIQUE}"
+PARENT_DESCRIPTION = f"sensitive-parent-description-{_UNIQUE}"
+CHILD_NAME = f"VBAC Child {_UNIQUE}"
+CHILD_DESCRIPTION = f"sensitive-child-description-{_UNIQUE}"
+
+GET_CONTAINER = """
+query container($urn: String!) {
+  container(urn: $urn) {
+    urn
+    properties {
+      name
+      description
+    }
+  }
+}
+"""
+
+GET_PARENT_CONTAINERS = """
+query parentContainersOnContainer($urn: String!) {
+  container(urn: $urn) {
+    urn
+    parentContainers {
+      count
+      containers {
+        urn
+        properties {
+          name
+          description
+        }
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+"""
+
+CONTAINER_VIEW_POLICY_PREFIXES = ["Test VIEW container"]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module", autouse=True)
+def container_view_auth_setup(graph_client, auth_session):
+    yield from _container_view_auth_setup_impl(graph_client, auth_session)
+
+
+def _container_view_auth_setup_impl(graph_client, auth_session):
+    if not is_view_authorization_enabled(auth_session):
+        pytest.skip(
+            "VIEW_AUTHORIZATION_ENABLED is false; "
+            "container view authorization tests require view authorization"
+        )
+
+    graph_client.emit_mcp(
+        MetadataChangeProposalWrapper(
+            entityUrn=PARENT_CONTAINER_URN,
+            aspect=ContainerPropertiesClass(
+                name=PARENT_NAME,
+                description=PARENT_DESCRIPTION,
+            ),
+        )
+    )
+    graph_client.emit_mcp(
+        MetadataChangeProposalWrapper(
+            entityUrn=CHILD_CONTAINER_URN,
+            aspect=ContainerPropertiesClass(
+                name=CHILD_NAME,
+                description=CHILD_DESCRIPTION,
+            ),
+        )
+    )
+    graph_client.emit_mcp(
+        MetadataChangeProposalWrapper(
+            entityUrn=CHILD_CONTAINER_URN,
+            aspect=ContainerClass(container=PARENT_CONTAINER_URN),
+        )
+    )
+    wait_for_writes_to_sync(mcp_only=True)
+
+    admin_session = get_frontend_session()
+    clear_polices(admin_session, name_prefixes=CONTAINER_VIEW_POLICY_PREFIXES)
+    set_base_platform_privileges_policy_status("INACTIVE", admin_session)
+    set_view_dataset_sensitive_info_policy_status("INACTIVE", admin_session)
+    set_view_entity_profile_privileges_policy_status("INACTIVE", admin_session)
+    wait_for_writes_to_sync(mae_only=True)
+
+    admin_session = create_user(admin_session, TEST_USER_EMAIL, TEST_USER_PASSWORD)
+    yield
+
+    remove_user(admin_session, TEST_USER_URN)
+    clear_polices(admin_session, name_prefixes=CONTAINER_VIEW_POLICY_PREFIXES)
+    set_base_platform_privileges_policy_status("ACTIVE", admin_session)
+    set_view_dataset_sensitive_info_policy_status("ACTIVE", admin_session)
+    set_view_entity_profile_privileges_policy_status("ACTIVE", admin_session)
+    wait_for_writes_to_sync(mae_only=True)
+
+    for urn in [CHILD_CONTAINER_URN, PARENT_CONTAINER_URN]:
+        try:
+            graph_client.hard_delete_entity(urn=urn)
+        except Exception:
+            logger.warning("Failed to delete %s during cleanup", urn)
+
+
+def _is_description_stripped(props: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
+    description = props.get("description")
+    return description != PARENT_DESCRIPTION and description in (None, "")
+
+
+@with_test_retry(max_attempts=10)
+def _assert_container_description_stripped(
+    email: str, password: str, urn: str
+) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """Retry until policy cache reflects revoked VIEW (description field-stripped)."""
+    user_session = login_as(email, password)
+    payload = {"query": GET_CONTAINER, "variables": {"urn": urn}}
+    response = user_session.post(f"{get_frontend_url()}/api/v2/graphql", json=payload)
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    res = response.json()
+    container = (res.get("data") or {}).get("container")
+    assert container is not None, res
+    assert container.get("urn") == urn, res
+    props = container.get("properties") or {}
+    assert props.get("name") == PARENT_NAME, res
+    assert _is_description_stripped(props), res
+    return res
+
+
+@with_test_retry(max_attempts=10)
+def _assert_container_description_visible(
+    email: str, password: str, urn: str
+) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    user_session = login_as(email, password)
+    payload = {"query": GET_CONTAINER, "variables": {"urn": urn}}
+    response = user_session.post(f"{get_frontend_url()}/api/v2/graphql", json=payload)
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    res = response.json()
+    container = (res.get("data") or {}).get("container")
+    assert container is not None, res
+    assert container.get("urn") == urn, res
+    props = container.get("properties") or {}
+    assert props.get("description") == PARENT_DESCRIPTION, res
+    return res
+
+
+@with_test_retry(max_attempts=10)
+def _assert_parent_container_description_stripped(
+    email: str, password: str
+) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], Dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Retry until hierarchy is present and parent description is field-stripped."""
+    user_session = login_as(email, password)
+    payload = {
+        "query": GET_PARENT_CONTAINERS,
+        "variables": {"urn": CHILD_CONTAINER_URN},
+    }
+    response = user_session.post(f"{get_frontend_url()}/api/v2/graphql", json=payload)
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    res = response.json()
+    container = (res.get("data") or {}).get("container")
+    assert container is not None, res
+    parents = (container.get("parentContainers") or {}).get("containers") or []
+    parent_by_urn = {entry.get("urn"): entry for entry in parents if entry}
+    assert PARENT_CONTAINER_URN in parent_by_urn, res
+    props = parent_by_urn[PARENT_CONTAINER_URN].get("properties") or {}
+    assert props.get("name") == PARENT_NAME, res
+    assert _is_description_stripped(props), res
+    return res, props
+
+
+@with_test_retry(max_attempts=10)
+def _assert_parent_container_description_visible(
+    email: str, password: str
+) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], Dict[str, Any]]:
+    user_session = login_as(email, password)
+    payload = {
+        "query": GET_PARENT_CONTAINERS,
+        "variables": {"urn": CHILD_CONTAINER_URN},
+    }
+    response = user_session.post(f"{get_frontend_url()}/api/v2/graphql", json=payload)
+    response.raise_for_status()
+    res = response.json()
+    container = (res.get("data") or {}).get("container")
+    assert container is not None, res
+    parents = (container.get("parentContainers") or {}).get("containers") or []
+    parent_by_urn = {entry.get("urn"): entry for entry in parents if entry}
+    assert PARENT_CONTAINER_URN in parent_by_urn, res
+    props = parent_by_urn[PARENT_CONTAINER_URN].get("properties") or {}
+    assert props.get("description") == PARENT_DESCRIPTION, res
+    return res, props
+
+
+def test_container_field_stripped_without_view():
+    """Unauthorized container loads keep the real URN but strip description."""
+    _assert_container_description_stripped(
+        TEST_USER_EMAIL, TEST_USER_PASSWORD, PARENT_CONTAINER_URN
+    )
+
+
+def test_container_visible_with_view(auth_session):
+    """VIEW_ENTITY_PAGE on the container restores the description."""
+    admin_session = get_frontend_session()
+    policy_urn = create_metadata_policy(
+        admin_session,
+        name=f"Test VIEW container {_UNIQUE}",
+        description="Grant VIEW_ENTITY_PAGE on parent container",
+        privileges=["VIEW_ENTITY_PAGE", "GET_ENTITY_PRIVILEGE"],
+        user_urn=TEST_USER_URN,
+        resource_urn=PARENT_CONTAINER_URN,
+    )
+
+    try:
+        _assert_container_description_visible(
+            TEST_USER_EMAIL, TEST_USER_PASSWORD, PARENT_CONTAINER_URN
+        )
+    finally:
+        remove_policy(policy_urn, admin_session)
+
+
+def test_parent_containers_returns_stripped_unauthorized_parent():
+    """parentContainers keeps unauthorized parents as field-stripped stubs."""
+    _assert_parent_container_description_stripped(TEST_USER_EMAIL, TEST_USER_PASSWORD)
+
+
+def test_parent_containers_visible_with_view_on_parent(auth_session):
+    """VIEW on the parent restores description via parentContainers stubs."""
+    admin_session = get_frontend_session()
+    policy_urn = create_metadata_policy(
+        admin_session,
+        name=f"Test VIEW container parent {_UNIQUE}",
+        description="Grant VIEW_ENTITY_PAGE on parent for parentContainers",
+        privileges=["VIEW_ENTITY_PAGE", "GET_ENTITY_PRIVILEGE"],
+        user_urn=TEST_USER_URN,
+        resource_urn=PARENT_CONTAINER_URN,
+    )
+
+    try:
+        _assert_parent_container_description_visible(
+            TEST_USER_EMAIL, TEST_USER_PASSWORD
+        )
+    finally:
+        remove_policy(policy_urn, admin_session)

primary.body:
## Summary
- Make `container` and `schemaField` view-restricted by default when VBAC is enabled (`container` no longer `viewUnrestricted` in the registry; stock `_ADD` omits `document` / `schemaField` / `container`)
- Field-strip unauthorized GraphQL container entity loads via `ContainerMapper` / `AuthorizationUtils.restrictEntity`, keeping real URNs in the hierarchy cache
- Update policies / env-var / updating-datahub docs and add `ViewAuthorizationConfigurationTest`
- Add smoke sibling `test_container_view_auth.py` (global_policy_mutator; skips unless `VIEW_AUTHORIZATION_ENABLED`)

## Test plan
- [ ] Unit: `ViewAuthorizationConfigurationTest` passes
- [ ] Smoke (VBAC on): `tests/authorization/test_container_view_auth.py` — field-strip without VIEW; full description with VIEW; parentContainers stubs
- [ ] With `VIEW_AUTHORIZATION_ENABLED=true`, unauthorized container GraphQL loads return field-stripped stubs (real URN retained)
- [ ] ParentContainers breadcrumbs still resolve hierarchy without rewriting cache entries to restricted URNs
- [ ] Confirm stock unrestricted overlays do not include `document`, `schemaField`, or `container`
- [ ] Docs render correctly for policies / env vars / updating-datahub entries

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Overview**
> **VBAC default for containers:** `container` no longer has `viewUnrestricted: true` in `entity-registry.yml`, and stock `VIEW_UNRESTRICTED_ENTITY_TYPES_ADD` explicitly omits `document`, `schemaField`, and `container` (docs and `application.yaml` comments updated accordingly).
> 
> **GraphQL behavior:** `ContainerMapper` now applies `AuthorizationUtils.restrictEntity` when the actor lacks **View Entity Page**, matching other entity mappers. Unauthorized `container(urn)` responses keep the real URN/name but strip sensitive fields (e.g. description). `ParentContainersResolver` documents that unauthorized ancestors are still included as field-stripped stubs rather than dropped or replaced with restricted URNs.
> 
> **Tests:** `ViewAuthorizationConfigurationTest` asserts the three types are absent from stock `_ADD`; new smoke module `test_container_view_auth.py` covers direct loads and `parentContainers` with and without VIEW grants (requires `VIEW_AUTHORIZATION_ENABLED`).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c9e7697d96f5d2827796dfe3cb2d764c2acb6533. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

tenant. routers/auth_router.py already disables /auth/register with
this same message; this duplicate had never been deactivated.

+---
+description: Perform a structured peer code review for the EduTrack application, enforcing Clean Architecture, CQRS, security rules, and project conventions.
+---
+
+# EduTrack Code Review
+
+You are a senior .NET / Angular developer performing a peer code review on the **EduTrack** educational tracking system. Produce structured, professional, and actionable feedback aligned with the project's architecture and team standards.
+
+EduTrack uses **Clean Architecture** (`Domain` -> `Application` -> `Infrastructure` -> `Api`), **CQRS via MediatR**, **EF Core + PostgreSQL**, **Repository + Unit of Work**, **AutoMapper**, and **FluentValidation** on the backend, and **Angular + TypeScript** on the frontend.
+
+Consult `.github/instructions/security.instructions.md` and `CLAUDE.md` / `.github/copilot-instructions.md` for the full set of enforced rules before reviewing.
+
+## Input
+
+The user will provide code file(s), a pull request, a diff, or a code snippet. If no code is supplied, ask for it before reviewing.
+
+If important context is missing (how a handler is called, related entities, configuration values), use available tools to gather it rather than guessing. Clearly state anything that cannot be determined.
+
+## Review Criteria
+
+Evaluate the code against every applicable criterion below.
+
+### 1. Clean Architecture boundaries
+- Does dependency flow inward only (`Api` -> `Application` -> `Domain`; `Infrastructure` implements `Domain` interfaces)?
+- Is `DbContext` used directly in an Application handler? (Violation — must go through `IUnitOfWork`.)
+- Does the `Domain` layer contain any infrastructure or framework concerns?
+
+### 2. CQRS & MediatR conventions
+- Are commands suffixed `Command` and queries suffixed `Query`?
+- Does every command / query have a corresponding `Handler` and a `Validator`?
+- Is business logic leaking into controllers instead of living in handlers?
+
+### 3. Naming & structure conventions
+- Entities: singular PascalCase (`Student`, not `Students`)
+- DTOs: suffix `Dto` (`StudentDto`)
+- Interfaces: prefix `I` (`IStudentRepository`)
+- Handlers: suffix `Handler`; Validators: suffix `Validator`
+
+### 4. Security (OWASP Top 10 — see `security.instructions.md`)
+- No raw SQL string interpolation; EF Core LINQ or parameterized `FromSqlRaw` only.
+- All controller actions decorated with `[Authorize]` unless explicitly public.
+- No secrets, connection strings, or API keys hardcoded; use `IConfiguration` / environment variables.
+- CORS not set to `AllowAnyOrigin()` in production; Swagger gated to Development only.
+- No PII (email, date of birth, phone) in log output.
+- No raw exception messages or stack traces returned to clients; use `ProblemDetails` (RFC 7807).
+- Angular: no `innerHTML` with untrusted data; no manual token attachment per request.
+- Tokens not stored in `localStorage`; HTTP errors handled in services, not components.
+
+### 5. Validation
+- Is a `FluentValidation` validator present for every new command / query?
+- Is input validated at the API boundary before reaching the Application layer?
+- Are `Guid` route parameters constrained with `{id:guid}`?
+
+### 6. Data access & performance
+- Are queries using appropriate projections (`.Select(...)`) to avoid over-fetching?
+- Are `async` / `await` and `CancellationToken` used throughout repository and handler methods?
+- Are there N+1 query risks (missing `.Include(...)` or unintended lazy loading)?
+
+### 7. Error handling & logging
+- Is `GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware` relied upon, rather than silent `catch` blocks?
+- Is structured logging used — `_logger.LogInformation("Entity {Id} created", id)` — with no string interpolation?
+- Are logs free of sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII)?
+
+### 8. AutoMapper usage
+- Are mappings defined in an Application-layer `Profile` class?
+- Are there any manual property-by-property mappings that should use AutoMapper?
+
+### 9. Testing
+- Are xUnit + Moq unit tests present or implied for new handlers, validators, and repositories?
+- Are happy-path, not-found, and validation-failure scenarios covered?
+
+### 10. Frontend (Angular / TypeScript)
+- Are `HttpClient` interceptors used for auth headers rather than per-request token attachment?
+- Are HTTP errors handled in services, not in components?
+- Is Angular's `DomSanitizer` used for any dynamic HTML?
+
+## Output Format
+
+Omit sections that have no findings.
+
+- **Code Review Summary**: 1–2 sentence overall assessment, key strengths, key concerns.
+- **Architecture & Convention Violations**: Clean Architecture boundary breaches, CQRS or naming violations.
+- **Findings**: grouped **High / Medium / Low**. Each finding: issue, location (file + function/line if known), impact, concrete recommendation.
+- **Security & Compliance Notes**: OWASP concerns, data sensitivity, auditability gaps.
+- **Testing Recommendations**: missing test cases, untested edge cases.
+- **Suggested Improvements**: optional refactors with a short rationale — only when clearly beneficial.

commit.message:
Escape LDAP user filter (#501)

Special characters within the username inserted into an LDAP search
request are not escaped. This could allow the logic of the LDAP query
used to get a user to be manipulated.

This change escapes any special characters within the username being
looked up within LDAP.

Signed-off-by: Mark S. Lewis <Mark.S.Lewis@outlook.com>

-The vulnerability arises when frameworks bind req.body directly onto persistent entities. Below are common mistakes and minimal, secure patterns.
+**Nested relation / tenant hijack**

+# DIFF — vulnerable vs. fixed
+
+`vulnerable/app.py` and `fixed/app.py` differ in exactly two places — one added import and the line that builds the search filter. `GET /` (the warning banner), the LDAP connection and the service-account bind, the response handling, the `Dockerfile`, and `requirements.txt` are identical between the two versions, as are the shared `ldap/` image and its seed. (This atom is API-only — there are no templates.)
+
+## The fix — escape the filter metacharacters
+
+```diff
++from ldap3.utils.conv import escape_filter_chars
+ ...
+     user = body.get("user", "")
+     password = body.get("password", "")
+-    # VULNERABLE: user/password are concatenated straight into the LDAP search
+-    # filter. ... the metacharacters * ( ) \ are syntax, not data ...
+-    filt = f"(&(uid={user})(userPassword={password}))"
++    # FIXED: escape the RFC 4515 filter metacharacters in every untrusted value
++    # before building the filter. * ( ) \ become literal data (\2a \28 \29 \5c) ...
++    filt = f"(&(uid={escape_filter_chars(user)})(userPassword={escape_filter_chars(password)}))"
+     print("LDAP search filter:", filt, flush=True)
+     conn = Connection(server, BIND_DN, BIND_PW, auto_bind=True)
+     conn.search(PEOPLE_DN, filt, search_scope=SUBTREE, attributes=["uid"])
+```
+
+The vulnerable view concatenates `user` and `password` straight into the filter string. The fixed view runs each value through `escape_filter_chars` first, which replaces the RFC 4515 metacharacters `*`, `(`, `)`, `\` (and NUL) with their escape sequences `\2a`, `\28`, `\29`, `\5c` before they reach the filter. A `*` sent as the password is then no longer the wildcard that turns `(userPassword=<value>)` into a presence test — it becomes the literal search `(userPassword=\2a)`, matching only an account whose password is literally the one-character string `*` (there is none), so the login is refused. The value is matched as a value again. It escapes **both** `user` and `password`: both are attacker-controlled and both land in the filter, so both are escaped at the point of use.
+
+## Why this fixes the bug
+
+An LDAP search filter is structure, and `ldap3` sends the filter string you hand it to the directory verbatim — it does not escape interpolated values for you. The vulnerable app builds the filter from raw input, so a metacharacter in the input becomes filter syntax. The fixed app guarantees every untrusted value is escaped before the filter is assembled, so the filter can only ever be the intended `(&(uid=<literal>)(userPassword=<literal>))` — two literal equality tests, with no room for a wildcard or a grafted-on clause. The benign case is unchanged: a real credential contains no metacharacters, so escaping is a no-op and it round-trips exactly as before. The root cause was never the character the attacker typed; it was concatenating untrusted input into the filter *as structure*, and escaping at the point of use is exactly its negation.
+
+## Validating or blocklisting characters is not the fix
+
+An experienced reader has a fix ready: "it's user input in a query — just restrict the characters, forbid `*` and parentheses in the `user` field." Whether you frame it as a blocklist of bad characters or an allowlist of good ones, it is the wrong shape. Policing the input's character set chases the form of the attack: alternate encodings, a metacharacter you forgot (`\`, NUL), a field that legitimately contains symbols, the next input you didn't think to filter. You stay one bypass behind, and you break real data that happens to contain a symbol.
+
+Escaping is different in kind: it says "whatever this value contains, treat all of it as data," and it lives at the **point of use** — the moment the value is placed into the filter — so there is nothing to keep up to date and no legitimate input it rejects. Escape at the sink; don't try to sanitize the source. (Same shape as the "named, not applied" notes in `ssti-jinja` and `nosql-injection-mongo`: name the control the reader reaches for, and show why it is not the fix.)
+
+## The honest design is a bind, not "the search matched"
+
+One design note, because it is the tempting deeper fix and this atom deliberately leaves it alone. Deciding auth by *searching* `(&(uid=...)(userPassword=...))` and trusting that a match means a valid login is fragile on its own — it is what lets a filter trick become an auth bypass. Real LDAP authentication is a **bind**: the app connects to the directory *as the user's own DN* with the supplied password, and whether that bind succeeds *is* the password check. The injection in this atom — a metacharacter in the search filter — cannot produce a bypass against a bind, because the directory verifies the password itself instead of counting search hits.
+
+So why keep the fragile design and only escape? Because switching to a bind changes the *design*, not the *vulnerability*. This atom isolates one flaw — untrusted input concatenated into a filter — and its minimal negation is to escape that input. Rewriting the login to bind would fix the injection only as a side effect of replacing the whole mechanism, which is exactly the kind of change that blurs what the lesson is. Name the better design; keep the diff to the cause. (Same spirit as the "hashing is orthogonal" note in `nosql-injection-mongo`.)
+
+## Same class as the Mongo NoSQL injection — opposite fix
+
+The finding is an authentication bypass: a crafted login as `admin` without the password, which is account takeover. That is the same ceiling as an auth bypass through SQL injection or NoSQL injection — and this atom is worth holding next to `nosql-injection-mongo` (22), because they are alike in impact and category and *nothing else*.
+
+| Axis | SQL injection (`sqli-union-basic`) | NoSQL injection (`nosql-injection-mongo`) | LDAP injection (this atom) |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Category | A03 — Injection | A03 — Injection | A03 — Injection |
+| Query language | SQL — a string of commands | a MongoDB query — a JSON document | an LDAP search filter — a string (RFC 4515) |
+| How input becomes structure | syntax spliced into a string (`' OR 1=1 --`) | type change: a string becomes an object carrying an operator (`{"$ne": null}`) | metacharacters in a concatenated filter string (`*` `(` `)` `\`) |
+| The fix | parameterize (bind variables) | force the type (reject non-strings) | escape the RFC 4515 metacharacters |
+| Is escaping the input the fix? | — | **no** — nothing to escape; the injection was a *type* | **yes** — the value carried filter *syntax* |
+
+Read that last row across. In the Mongo atom, escaping is precisely *not* the fix: the injection was a value that changed type into an operator, there was no string to escape, and the fix was to force the type. Here the injection is a metacharacter inside a string the app concatenated, so escaping is *exactly* the fix. Same class — untrusted input becoming query structure in a query language that isn't SQL — but *how* the input becomes structure decides the remedy, and the remedy that missed in 22 is the one that lands here. "One atom, one vulnerability" is about the cause, not the impact: `sqli-union-basic`, `nosql-injection-mongo`, and this atom can all end in a subverted query and a bypassed login, by three different roots.

+# DIFF — vulnerable vs. fixed
+
+`vulnerable/app.py` e `fixed/app.py` diferem em exatamente dois pontos — um import adicionado e a linha que monta o filtro de busca. O `GET /` (o banner de aviso), a conexão LDAP e o bind da service account, o tratamento da resposta, o `Dockerfile` e o `requirements.txt` são idênticos entre as duas versões, assim como a imagem compartilhada `ldap/` e seu seed. (Este átomo é API-only — não há templates.)
+
+## O fix — escapar os metacaracteres do filtro
+
+```diff
++from ldap3.utils.conv import escape_filter_chars
+ ...
+     user = body.get("user", "")
+     password = body.get("password", "")
+-    # VULNERABLE: user/password are concatenated straight into the LDAP search
+-    # filter. ... the metacharacters * ( ) \ are syntax, not data ...
+-    filt = f"(&(uid={user})(userPassword={password}))"
++    # FIXED: escape the RFC 4515 filter metacharacters in every untrusted value
++    # before building the filter. * ( ) \ become literal data (\2a \28 \29 \5c) ...
++    filt = f"(&(uid={escape_filter_chars(user)})(userPassword={escape_filter_chars(password)}))"
+     print("LDAP search filter:", filt, flush=True)
+     conn = Connection(server, BIND_DN, BIND_PW, auto_bind=True)
+     conn.search(PEOPLE_DN, filt, search_scope=SUBTREE, attributes=["uid"])
+```
+
+A view vulnerable concatena `user` e `password` direto na string do filtro. A view fixed passa cada valor antes pelo `escape_filter_chars`, que substitui os metacaracteres da RFC 4515 `*`, `(`, `)`, `\` (e NUL) pelas suas sequências de escape `\2a`, `\28`, `\29`, `\5c` antes de chegarem ao filtro. Um `*` mandado como senha deixa então de ser o curinga que transforma `(userPassword=<valor>)` num teste de presença — ele vira a busca literal `(userPassword=\2a)`, casando só uma conta cuja senha seja literalmente a string de um caractere `*` (não há nenhuma), então o login é recusado. O valor volta a ser casado como valor. O fix escapa **os dois**, `user` e `password`: ambos são controlados pelo atacante e ambos caem no filtro, então ambos são escapados no ponto de uso.
+
+## Por que isso corrige o bug
+
+Um filtro de busca LDAP é estrutura, e o `ldap3` manda a string de filtro que você entrega ao diretório verbatim — ele não escapa os valores interpolados por você. O app vulnerable monta o filtro a partir do input cru, então um metacaractere no input vira sintaxe do filtro. O app fixed garante que todo valor não-confiável é escapado antes de o filtro ser montado, então o filtro só pode ser o pretendido `(&(uid=<literal>)(userPassword=<literal>))` — duas igualdades literais, sem espaço para um curinga ou uma cláusula enxertada. O caso benigno fica inalterado: uma credencial real não tem metacaracteres, então escapar é um no-op e ela passa exatamente como antes. A causa raiz nunca foi o caractere que o atacante digitou; foi concatenar input não-confiável no filtro *como estrutura*, e escapar no ponto de uso é exatamente a negação disso.
+
+## Validar ou colocar caracteres numa blocklist não é o fix
+
+Um leitor experiente tem um fix na ponta da língua: "é input de usuário numa query — é só restringir os caracteres, proibir `*` e parênteses no campo `user`." Seja como uma blocklist de caracteres ruins ou uma allowlist dos bons, é a forma errada. Policiar o charset do input persegue a forma do ataque: encodings alternativos, um metacaractere que você esqueceu (`\`, NUL), um campo que legitimamente contém símbolos, o próximo input que você não pensou em filtrar. Você fica um bypass atrás, e quebra dado real que por acaso contém um símbolo.
+
+Escapar é diferente em natureza: ele diz "seja lá o que este valor contém, trate tudo como dado", e vive no **ponto de uso** — o momento em que o valor é colocado no filtro — então não há nada a manter atualizado e nenhum input legítimo que ele rejeite. Escape no sink; não tente sanitizar a source. (Mesma forma das notas "mencionável, não aplicada" do `ssti-jinja` e do `nosql-injection-mongo`: nomeie o controle que o leitor busca e mostre por que não é o fix.)
+
+## O desenho honesto é um bind, não "a busca casou"
+
+Uma nota de desenho, porque é o fix mais profundo e tentador e este átomo de propósito o deixa de lado. Decidir a auth *buscando* `(&(uid=...)(userPassword=...))` e confiar que um match significa um login válido é frágil por si só — é o que deixa um truque no filtro virar um bypass de auth. A autenticação LDAP de verdade é um **bind**: o app conecta ao diretório *como o próprio DN do usuário* com a senha fornecida, e o sucesso desse bind *é* a checagem de senha. A injeção deste átomo — um metacaractere no filtro de busca — não consegue produzir um bypass contra um bind, porque o diretório verifica a senha ele mesmo em vez de contar hits de busca.
+
+Então por que manter o desenho frágil e só escapar? Porque trocar para um bind muda o *desenho*, não a *vulnerabilidade*. Este átomo isola uma falha — input não-confiável concatenado num filtro — e sua negação mínima é escapar esse input. Reescrever o login para bind corrigiria a injeção só como efeito colateral de substituir o mecanismo inteiro, que é exatamente o tipo de mudança que borra qual é a lição. Nomeie o desenho melhor; mantenha o diff na causa. (Mesmo espírito da nota "hashing é ortogonal" do `nosql-injection-mongo`.)
+
+## Mesma classe do NoSQL injection do Mongo — fix oposto
+
+O finding é um bypass de autenticação: um login forjado como `admin` sem a senha, o que é account takeover. É o mesmo teto de um bypass de auth via SQL injection ou NoSQL injection — e vale pôr este átomo ao lado do `nosql-injection-mongo` (22), porque eles são parecidos em impacto e categoria e *nada mais*.
+
+| Eixo | SQL injection (`sqli-union-basic`) | NoSQL injection (`nosql-injection-mongo`) | LDAP injection (este átomo) |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Categoria | A03 — Injection | A03 — Injection | A03 — Injection |
+| Query-language | SQL — uma string de comandos | uma query MongoDB — um documento JSON | um filtro de busca LDAP — uma string (RFC 4515) |
+| Como o input vira estrutura | sintaxe emendada numa string (`' OR 1=1 --`) | mudança de tipo: uma string vira um objeto carregando um operador (`{"$ne": null}`) | metacaracteres numa string de filtro concatenada (`*` `(` `)` `\`) |
+| O fix | parametrizar (bind variables) | forçar o tipo (rejeitar não-string) | escapar os metacaracteres da RFC 4515 |
+| Escapar o input é o fix? | — | **não** — não há o que escapar; a injeção era um *tipo* | **sim** — o valor carregava *sintaxe* de filtro |
+
+Leia essa última linha de ponta a ponta. No átomo do Mongo, escapar é justamente *não* ser o fix: a injeção era um valor que mudava de tipo para um operador, não havia string para escapar, e o fix era forçar o tipo. Aqui a injeção é um metacaractere dentro de uma string que o app concatenou, então escapar é *exatamente* o fix. Mesma classe — input não-confiável virando estrutura de query numa query-language que não é SQL — mas *como* o input vira estrutura decide o remédio, e o remédio que errou no 22 é o que acerta aqui. "Um átomo = uma vuln" é sobre a causa, não sobre o impacto: `sqli-union-basic`, `nosql-injection-mongo` e este átomo podem todos terminar numa query subvertida e num login bypassado, por três causas diferentes.

+# ldap-injection — LDAP injection
+
+> ⚠️ Intentionally vulnerable. Run locally only. Never expose to the internet or a shared network.
+
+A minimal Flask + OpenLDAP lab for LDAP injection. A corporate-style login endpoint — `POST /login` — takes a `user` and a `password` and authenticates them against an LDAP directory: it builds a search filter and considers you logged in if the search returns anyone — `(&(uid=<user>)(userPassword=<password>))`. The catch is that an LDAP search filter is not inert text — it is **structure** (RFC 4515), and characters like `*`, `(`, `)` and `\` are *syntax*, not data. The endpoint pastes whatever the client sent straight into that filter, so those metacharacters are interpreted as filter logic. Send `*` as the password and the filter becomes `(&(uid=admin)(userPassword=*))` — "an `admin` that simply *has* a password" — and you log in as `admin` without knowing it.
+
+The lesson is that the root cause is **concatenating untrusted input into the filter without escaping it**: the value stops being a value and becomes filter structure. The fix is not to validate or blocklist "weird" characters — it is to **escape the RFC 4515 metacharacters** (`escape_filter_chars`) in every untrusted value before the filter is built, so `*` `(` `)` `\` turn into literal data (`\2a` `\28` `\29` `\5c`) and the filter stays the one the code intended.
+
+> **Theory primer:** Read [PortSwigger: LDAP injection](https://portswigger.net/kb/issues/00100500_ldap-injection)
+> before working through this atom, and skim the [OWASP LDAP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/LDAP_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)
+> for the defense. The atoms in this repo show *how* a vulnerability happens in
+> code; those references explain *what* it is and why it matters.
+
+## Stack note — a real OpenLDAP directory
+
+Unlike the SQL injection atoms (`sqli-union-basic` and its blind siblings), which embed SQLite as a file inside the process, this atom needs a real directory *server*: OpenLDAP. So the lab runs **three containers** — one shared `ldap`, plus `vulnerable` and `fixed`, both querying the same seeded directory. The `ldap` service has **no host port**: it is reachable only on the compose's internal network (`ldap://ldap:389`), never published to your machine — only the two apps bind to `127.0.0.1`. The apps talk to it with **`ldap3`**, a pure-Python LDAP client (chosen over `python-ldap` so there is no native `libldap`/build toolchain to install). The directory is seeded with two fake users (`admin`, `jdoe`) whose passwords are stored in plaintext — a lab simplification so the naive `(userPassword=<value>)` match works; password storage is orthogonal to the LDAP injection fix (see `DIFF.md`). The apps bind as a **low-privilege service account** (`cn=svc`), not the directory admin, so the bypass you will see is LDAP injection and not an over-privileged connection.
+
+## API only — no HTML, no browser
+
+This atom has no web UI: no templates, no landing page, every response is JSON. You drive it entirely from **Burp Suite (Repeater)** or `curl`, and the proof is the login response itself — nothing executes in a browser. `WALKTHROUGH.md` works exclusively from Burp.
+
+## Run
+
+From the repo root:
+
+```bash
+./atom up ldap-injection
+```
+
+- Vulnerable API: `http://127.0.0.1:8028`
+- Fixed API: `http://127.0.0.1:8128`
+
+`GET /` returns a warning banner; the entry point is `POST /login` (see `WALKTHROUGH.md`). The `ldap` container is never published — only the two apps are. Stop with `./atom down ldap-injection`. If you prefer raw Docker: `cd atoms/A03-injection/ldap-injection && docker compose up --build`.
+
+## What to read next
+
+1. [`WALKTHROUGH.md`](./WALKTHROUGH.md) — step-by-step exploitation via Burp Suite (API-only; no browser track).
+2. [`DIFF.md`](./DIFF.md) — commented diff between `vulnerable/` and `fixed/`.
+
+## Fixed version
+
+The patched app on port 8128 serves the same login against the same directory. It adds one thing — `escape_filter_chars` around `user` and `password` before the filter is built — and changes nothing else. Replay the walkthrough against it: the real string credential still logs in with `200`, and the `*` payload that bypassed the vulnerable app now returns `401`, because the metacharacter is escaped to the literal `\2a` and can no longer be filter structure.

+# ldap-injection — LDAP injection
+
+> ⚠️ Intentionally vulnerable. Run locally only. Never expose to the internet or a shared network.
+
+Um lab mínimo em Flask + OpenLDAP para LDAP injection. Um endpoint de login corporativo — `POST /login` — recebe um `user` e um `password` e os autentica contra um diretório LDAP: monta um filtro de busca e considera você logado se a busca retorna alguém — `(&(uid=<user>)(userPassword=<password>))`. O detalhe é que um filtro de busca LDAP não é texto inerte — é **estrutura** (RFC 4515), e caracteres como `*`, `(`, `)` e `\` são *sintaxe*, não dado. O endpoint cola o que o cliente mandou direto nesse filtro, então esses metacaracteres são interpretados como lógica do filtro. Mande `*` como senha e o filtro vira `(&(uid=admin)(userPassword=*))` — "um `admin` que simplesmente *tem* uma senha" — e você loga como `admin` sem conhecê-la.
+
+A lição é que a causa raiz é **concatenar input não-confiável no filtro sem escapá-lo**: o valor deixa de ser valor e vira estrutura do filtro. O fix não é validar nem colocar caracteres "estranhos" numa blocklist — é **escapar os metacaracteres da RFC 4515** (`escape_filter_chars`) em cada valor não-confiável antes de montar o filtro, para que `*` `(` `)` `\` virem dado literal (`\2a` `\28` `\29` `\5c`) e o filtro continue sendo o que o código pretendia.
+
+> **Teoria primeiro:** Leia [PortSwigger: LDAP injection](https://portswigger.net/kb/issues/00100500_ldap-injection)
+> antes de fazer este átomo, e passe os olhos no [OWASP LDAP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/LDAP_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)
+> para a defesa. Os átomos deste repo mostram *como* uma vulnerabilidade
+> acontece no código; essas referências explicam *o que* ela é e por que importa.
+
+## Nota de stack — um diretório OpenLDAP de verdade
+
+Diferente dos átomos de SQL injection (`sqli-union-basic` e os irmãos blind), que embutem o SQLite como um arquivo dentro do processo, este átomo precisa de um *servidor* de diretório de verdade: OpenLDAP.
